reason: DETERMINACY without the knee encoders HOLDS for this design, under one condition: K must stay on its law. This was re-run on this design, model and verifier unchanged, with the frozen protocol and the null-space Jacobian of the loop J1-K-J2-J3-pin a-pin b-GH(3R). Frames were checked from both members of every joint (max error 7e-6 mm). With K slaved by its lin law (slope dK/dq2 = 1.6232 regressed from the taken poses, residual 0.0; 0 on stop A), mobility is 3 at every taken pose. The 3 hub rates fix every passive coordinate, the knee pins and GH included. Fit bench (188 taken poses): sigma_min min 0.310, p5 0.311, condition max 2.75; knee-pin rate per hub rate up to 2.36. Exact bench numbers are in the .md and the remeasure file. Reference skin-normal-3r-pin-knee: sigma_min >= 0.39, condition <= 2.3, so this design is a little worse conditioned but nowhere near singular (0 poses under 0.05). The condition: with K free (no law), mobility is 4 and the hub encoders alone have sigma_min 0 at every pose. A K lag or drive lift-off is then invisible to the 3 encoders and goes straight into the estimated arm pose. K is held on its law only by one 0.08 N.m clock spring keeping the drive in compression, and R17 (lift-off / K lag) has never run on this design (M5). So 'no encoders needed' is proven at the kinematic level only, not for the real spring-held drive. Not gamed: the premise holds at every taken pose in the model.
